The premise in the query is not part of the original node2vec method: node2vec does not use Spiking Neural Networks, leaky integrate-and-fire membrane potentials, or spike-timing-dependent plasticity. In the published node2vec algorithm, node transitions are generated by a biased second-order random walk, and the learned objective is to optimize node embeddings from sampled walk contexts using a skip-gram-style model.

So, there is no spike-timing-dependent plasticity rule in node2vec as originally defined. If one were to build a hypothetical SNN-based variant of node2vec, an STDP rule would typically mean that synaptic weights are increased when a presynaptic spike precedes a postsynaptic spike within a short time window and decreased when the order is reversed. In that speculative setting, the timing of spikes would modulate transition probabilities or edge weights, but that would be an extension beyond node2vec rather than a property of the original algorithm.

In short: original node2vec uses biased random walks and skip-gram optimization, not SNN dynamics or STDP.
